title: Automated Fintech Ledger Reconciliation
business: A mid-sized fintech firm managing high-frequency transaction ledgers.
problem: Engineers frequently introduce regression bugs during manual reconciliation logic updates, leading to inconsistent account balances and costly manual audits.
solution: The firm adopts Superpowers to enforce a rigorous TDD workflow and subagent-driven code reviews, ensuring that every logic change is validated against failing tests before integration.
steps: Initiate a /brainstorming session to map edge cases for ledger reconciliation.
Define test suites using the TDD module to ensure all new logic triggers a red-green-refactor cycle.
Deploy subagent-driven development to draft implementation code.
Utilize the built-in code-reviewer agent to validate the implementation against architectural principles.
Finalize the module only after the code-reviewer agent confirms compliance with the initial plan.
outcome: A more stable codebase where reconciliation logic is consistently verified by automated tests, significantly reducing the frequency of post-deployment balance discrepancies.
limitation: The framework enforces strict methodology, which can slow down rapid prototyping; developers can check for this by monitoring the time-to-first-commit during the TDD cycle.
